name: issue_fixed_command_sequence
description: Makes six calls to a lower-level routine in a fixed order, with constant argument triples and its own parameter passed through twice. It finally repeats an earlier return value, so it only replays a fixed sequence.

name: reset_state_when_flagged
description: Calls a lower-level routine with three constant arguments. When its flag argument is nonzero it also clears the shared global variable twice.

name: build_mode_dependent_packet
description: Stores a dispatch pointer, then makes a long series of calls to a lower-level routine with constant arguments. When the low seven bits of the shared global equal three, it builds a stack-frame parameter block and sends it through the dispatch pointer.

name: run_full_mode_packet_dispatch
description: Repeats the same pattern as its neighbour in a longer form: a fixed series of constant-argument calls, a mode test on the shared global, and a parameter block built on the stack and sent through the dispatch pointer when the mode is three and the flag is set.

name: send_mode_three_status_packet
description: Makes four calls through the dispatch pointer with constant arguments. When the mode field equals three and a flag is set, it also sends a stack-built parameter block.

name: dispatch_on_request_code
description: Branches on a one-byte request code. Code zero calls two routines when two flags are nonzero, and code one builds a stack message of constant words and sends it through the dispatch pointer.

name: send_code_one_message
description: Handles only request code one: when a flag is set and a call returns zero, it builds a stack message of constant words and sends it through the dispatch pointer, then makes a follow-up call.

name: send_code_two_message
description: Handles request code two by building a stack message from the shared global and a register argument, then sending it through the dispatch pointer. It makes a follow-up call when a second flag is set.

name: compute_masked_table_lookup
description: Stores three arguments into shared globals and calls a lower-level routine. A nonzero result is added to a byte from a lookup table and masked to five bits, while a zero result yields the constant twenty.

name: store_constant_twenty
description: Stores the constant twenty in the shared global variable and returns it.

name: step_index_through_table
description: Adjusts the shared index by a fixed amount chosen by which range it falls in: below zero, zero to nine, or ten and above. It then replaces a nonzero index with a byte-table entry, calls a lower-level routine and returns the index.

name: advance_index_via_pointer
description: Adjusts the shared index by a range-dependent offset, then replaces the value behind a pointer with a byte-table entry. It calls a lower-level routine and returns the pointed-to value.

name: adjust_index_two_range
description: Subtracts three from the shared index when it is at least three, or adds three when it is negative. It replaces the pointed-to value with a table entry, calls a lower-level routine and returns the pointed-to value.

name: step_index_down_by_three
description: When the shared index is greater than two, subtracts three from it, replaces the pointed-to value with a table entry and calls a lower-level routine. It returns the pointed-to value.

name: offset_index_by_table_entry
description: Returns the index plus an entry from a three-element table when both inputs are in range. A negative table selector returns the one's complement of the index, and out-of-range inputs return thirty.

name: offset_register_by_table_entry
description: Returns its register value plus a table entry chosen by a second register. A negative selector returns the one's complement of the value instead.

name: add_table_entry_to_value
description: Returns its first register-passed value plus the table entry selected by the second register, with no range check.

name: clamp_negative_result_to_thirty
description: Calls a sibling routine with its two parameters and returns the result, replacing any negative result with thirty.

name: call_routine_twice
description: Invokes the same lower-level routine twice in succession with no arguments and does nothing else.

name: store_chained_routine_result
description: Calls a lower-level routine with no arguments, passes its result into a second call, and stores that second result in the shared global variable.

name: dispatch_six_byte_table_entry
description: Chooses one of several six-byte table entries from the shared global code, computing an offset from a second value for some codes. It passes the selected entry and a length of six to a lower-level routine, and returns at once for negative codes.

name: call_if_code_twenty_four
description: Calls a lower-level routine only when a register word equals twenty-four, and does nothing otherwise.

name: call_single_routine
description: Calls a lower-level routine once with no arguments and returns.

name: call_routine_once_bare
description: Calls a lower-level routine once with no arguments and returns. It is a bare trampoline with no other work.

name: call_with_rounded_global
description: Passes the shared global variable, rounded down to a multiple of thirty-two and truncated to a byte, to a lower-level routine.

name: add_signed_offset_to_global
description: Returns its argument plus the shared global variable, negating the argument first when the global is negative.

name: accumulate_signed_offset_into_global
description: Adds its argument to the shared global variable, negating the argument first when the global is negative. It stores the sum back into the global and returns it.

name: interpret_text_control_codes
description: Reads bytes from a stream and interprets two escape codes: one skips the next byte, and the other reads a subcommand. Subcommands call the lower-level routine with fixed values or a mode-dependent value, and code three restarts the loop.

name: interpret_control_codes_pointer
description: Reads the same kind of control-code stream as its neighbour, but through an address register rather than the shared global pointer. It also sets a flag byte to one after an escape is handled.

name: store_byte_no_op_clamp
description: Stores a byte into the target location and rewrites the same value if it equals minus seventy-one. The second write has no effect, so the routine is a plain byte store.

name: interpret_control_codes_entry
description: Shows the start of the same control-code stream reader used by its neighbours. Only a loop fragment is present, so its exact entry behaviour is partly visible.

name: return_without_action
description: Returns immediately with no body. It is an empty entry with no work to do.

name: call_with_argument_minus_seven
description: Passes its argument minus seven to a lower-level routine and returns.

name: load_indexed_global_byte
description: Copies the element at the given index of a shared array into the shared global variable. It returns that element, sign-extended from a byte.

name: compute_quarter_offset_from_position
description: Divides its argument plus sixty by sixty-three, keeps the low two bits of the quotient with sign handling, and returns that value minus one.

name: signed_bits_minus_one
description: Takes the low two bits of a register value with sign handling for negatives, and returns that result minus one.

name: low_two_bits_minus_one
description: Returns the low two bits of its register argument minus one, giving a result from minus one to two.

name: transfer_global_block_eighteen
description: Passes the address of the shared global variable as both source and destination, with a length of eighteen, to a lower-level routine. Three identical copies of this one-line wrapper appear in a row.

name: transfer_global_block_eighteen
description: Passes the address of the shared global variable as both source and destination, with a length of eighteen, to a lower-level routine. This is identical in body to its neighbouring wrappers.

name: transfer_global_block_eighteen
description: Passes the address of the shared global variable as both source and destination, with a length of eighteen, to a lower-level routine. This is identical in body to its neighbouring wrappers.

name: transfer_global_block_eighteen
description: Passes the address of the shared global variable as both source and destination, with a length of eighteen, to a lower-level routine. The body is identical to its neighbouring wrappers.

name: init_then_transfer_eighteen_block
description: Calls a lower-level routine with no arguments, then passes a fixed table address, the address of the shared global block and a length of eighteen to it.

name: init_then_transfer_eighteen_block
description: Calls a lower-level routine with no arguments, then passes a fixed table address, the address of the shared global block and a length of eighteen to it. The body matches its neighbouring routine.

name: init_then_transfer_block_reversed
description: Calls a lower-level routine with no arguments, then passes the shared global block, a fixed table address and a length of eighteen to it. Only the argument order differs from its neighbours.

name: store_fixed_size_constants
description: Writes four constants into shared variables in sequence: two zeros, then three hundred twenty and one hundred ninety-two.

name: is_allowed_code_value
description: Returns zero for zero and for the positive values nine, twelve, twenty, and twenty-six through twenty-nine. It returns one for any other positive value and for every negative value.

name: return_constant_zero
description: Returns zero with no other work.

name: call_with_global_triplicate
description: Passes the shared global variable, as a signed word, three times to a lower-level routine and returns its byte result.

name: compute_record_derived_value
description: Looks up a record for the shared index, and yields zero if the index is minus one or no record matches. It halves two ten-bit fields from the record with rounding, combines them with the constant fifty-eight, and stores the result.

name: compute_clamped_record_offset
description: Looks up a record and derives a half-rounded value from its ten-bit fields, as its neighbour does. It clamps the result to zero when it exceeds one hundred ninety-one, then passes it to a lower-level routine.

name: derive_clamped_position_value
description: Derives a value from a half-rounded global plus the constant fifty-eight and clamps results above one hundred ninety-one to zero. It runs the result through two lower-level calls and replaces a result of minus one with three.

name: derive_clamped_value_from_registers
description: Halves its first register argument, adds the constant fifty-eight and the second register, and clamps results above one hundred ninety-one to zero. It then runs them through two lower-level calls, replacing a minus-one result with three.

name: derive_clamped_value_with_threshold
description: Computes a value from its first register argument using the same offset and clamp as its neighbours. It then repeats the lower-level calls and applies a threshold of ten before a final adjustment.

name: clamp_result_to_nine
description: Passes a value through two lower-level calls and replaces the result with nine when the first result is ten or more. When bit five is set it adds and then removes four, which leaves the value unchanged.

name: pass_through_bit_five_check
description: Passes the shared global variable through a lower-level routine. When bit five of the result is set it adds and then subtracts four, which leaves the value unchanged.

name: forward_no_arg_result
description: Calls a lower-level routine with no arguments and passes its result to a second lower-level routine.

name: return_global_or_thirteen
description: Calls a lower-level routine with its parameter and returns the shared global variable, or thirteen when that variable is zero.

name: validate_and_select_entry
description: Tests conditions on the shared value and a lookup table: a byte range check, a result equal to twenty, and the codes fifty and fifty-one. When they pass, it stores a table entry into the shared variable.

name: select_entry_then_compare_seven
description: Applies the same conditional table-entry selection as its neighbour. It then subtracts four from the shared value and checks whether a further lookup returns seven.

name: scale_code_when_allowed
description: When the code is seven or twelve and excluded combinations do not apply, it multiplies the shared value by thirty-two after adding one. Otherwise it calls lower-level routines and checks the results against twenty and twelve.

name: scale_value_when_codes_match
description: Makes two lower-level calls on the shared value. It multiplies the value by thirty-two when a register argument matches it and the call results equal twenty or twelve.

name: increment_when_result_is_five
description: Calls a lower-level routine and adds one to the shared value when the result equals five.

name: adjust_code_and_dispatch
description: Normalises the shared value to a signed word and decrements it when it lies between one hundred thirty-four and one hundred forty-nine or equals two, three, four or six. It then passes the value to a lower-level routine.

name: adjust_code_from_record_bytes
description: Loads the shared value from two bytes of a record addressed by an address register. It decrements the value under the same range and code test as its neighbour, then passes it to a lower-level routine.

name: stub_no_op_assignments
description: Assigns the shared variable to itself repeatedly and returns, so it has no visible effect.

name: stub_self_assignment_run
description: Assigns the shared variable to itself repeatedly and returns, with no visible effect. It is identical in body to its neighbour.

name: classify_code_and_emit_calls
description: Returns at once for one specific code. Otherwise it sets the shared value from which listed ranges or values the code falls in, and makes several lower-level calls with fixed arguments.

name: classify_code_and_emit_sequence
description: Sets the shared value from the code's class, then makes the same fixed sequence of lower-level calls. It ends with a state update chosen by whether the value is zero.

name: emit_state_pair_after_adjust
description: Adjusts the shared value by eleven, or by fifteen when it is zero, or sends a minus-five argument for one special code. It then selects one of two state values and makes fixed lower-level calls.

name: decrement_and_emit_state_pair
description: Subtracts eleven from the shared value, or fifteen when it is zero, and calls a lower-level routine with five. It then selects one of two state values and makes fixed lower-level calls.

name: set_state_six_one_call
description: Stores six and then one in the shared variable, then makes three fixed lower-level calls, the middle one with argument five.

name: apply_table_offset_and_mark
description: When the shared value passes one of several conditions, it reads a table entry indexed by its low six bits. It calls lower-level routines with that entry, adds a second table byte to the result, sets the value to one, and calls a routine with three.

name: load_word_table_entry
description: Loads the shared variable from a word-sized table entry at the index given by its argument.

name: load_word_table_entry
description: Loads the shared variable from a word-sized table entry at the index given by its argument. It is identical in body to its neighbouring routine.

name: bracket_call_with_parameter
description: Calls a lower-level routine with no arguments, then with its parameter, then with no arguments again.

name: bracket_call_with_parameter
description: Calls a lower-level routine with no arguments, then with its parameter, then with no arguments again. It is identical in body to its neighbouring routine.

name: bracket_fixed_value_sequence
description: Calls a lower-level routine with no arguments and with the constant one hundred six, and stores one hundred forty-four in the shared variable between those calls.

name: store_constant_set_and_call
description: Stores the constants twenty-four, one hundred ninety-nine, one hundred sixty-seven and two hundred fifty-five into the shared variable in turn. It then calls a lower-level routine with one hundred five and once with no arguments.

name: store_pair_constants_and_call
description: Calls a lower-level routine with no arguments, stores one hundred thirty-six and one hundred sixty-four into the shared variable, then calls with one hundred nine and with no arguments.

name: set_global_164_after_call
description: Calls a lower-level routine with no arguments, subtracts two from the shared variable, then sets it to one hundred sixty-four.

name: store_constant_set_then_call
description: Stores five, one hundred twenty, one hundred sixty-six and two hundred fifty-five into the shared variable in turn. It then calls a lower-level routine with ninety-four and once with no arguments.

name: store_alt_constants_and_call
description: Stores six, one hundred ninety-eight, one hundred sixty-six and two hundred fifty-five into the shared variable, then calls a lower-level routine with ninety-five and once with no arguments.

name: store_constants_one_call
description: Stores zero, one hundred ninety-eight, one hundred sixty-four and two hundred fifty-five into the shared variable, then calls a lower-level routine with one and once with no arguments.

name: alternate_two_slot_update
description: Runs twice, toggling an index between two slots of a shared table. Each pass replaces the chosen slot with a lower-level routine's result and then calls a lower-level routine with that slot's value offset by thirteen and the constant one hundred sixteen.

name: alternate_two_slot_loop_registers
description: Loops over a counter register, toggling between two slots of a table addressed by registers. Each pass replaces the chosen slot with a lower-level routine's result and calls a lower-level routine with the constant one hundred sixteen and slot values.

name: cycle_index_and_send_frame
description: Advances the shared index modulo three and returns if the result exceeds six. Otherwise it passes a stack parameter block of fixed words to a lower-level routine, and when the index is nonzero it sends a second block built the same way.

name: emit_paired_entries_under_seven
description: Stores the upper word of a register into a pointed-to slot. When the shared index is below seven it makes a lower-level call with a slot offset of ten, then a second call with an offset of two when the index is nonzero.

name: make_paired_entry_calls
description: Calls a lower-level routine with fixed constants and a slot-derived offset of ten. When the shared index is nonzero it calls again with an offset of two.

name: call_nonzero_word_argument
description: Calls a lower-level routine with zero and its word argument, but only when that argument is nonzero.

name: call_zero_and_register_word
description: Calls a lower-level routine with a zero and the word held in a data register.

name: call_with_two_zeros
description: Calls a lower-level routine with two zero arguments.

name: advance_cycle_index_and_call
description: Advances a per-slot index in a six-byte record modulo five. It then calls a lower-level routine with two fields of that record and the byte selected by the new index.

name: reset_state_sequence_with_constants
description: Calls lower-level routines with a block address, a parameter and the constant eight. It then stores one, zero, three and four in turn, repeats four twice, and makes one final call.

name: handle_pause_state_polling
description: Reads a state value and loops while a pause flag is set, returning minus three or minus one depending on the result. The routine references the text GAME PAUSED, so it is part of pause handling.

name: save_restore_global_around_check
description: Saves the shared variable and clears it, then calls a lower-level routine. It sets the variable to two hundred fifty-five when that call returns nonzero, makes one more call, clears a flag and restores the saved variable.

name: read_code_and_update_state
description: Reads a code byte. Code one hundred twenty-four drains bytes until a zero byte appears and returns minus one. Other codes update the shared state, with codes twelve and five handled specially, and call lower-level routines.

name: dispatch_byte_code_ranges
description: Sets a state flag, then checks a byte code against several ranges. Codes above eighty-six go through a switch, and each branch calls lower-level routines with fixed or stack-relative arguments.

name: dispatch_sound_status_codes
description: Dispatches on a byte code like its neighbour and makes lower-level calls for each branch. The routine references the strings MEGA DRIVE ENGAGED, SOUND OFF and SOUND ON, so it appears to handle sound-related status messages.

name: stub_bad_instruction_data
description: Contains only a bad-instruction marker, so no executable behaviour was recovered. The text it references is a printf-style format string of coordinate labels, and that string is the only evidence beyond the marker.

name: map_character_code_input
description: Handles a character or key code. Digit characters set a shared value from a base plus the digit, capped at fourteen, and codes in one high range are passed to a lower-level routine with that range offset removed. A flagged case ends with a call and two stores of twenty-four.

name: map_character_code_input_long
description: Longer variant of the character-code handler beside it. Digit codes set the shared value from a base plus the digit, capped at fourteen, and a high range is passed to a lower-level routine with its offset removed. It returns minus three.

name: branch_on_result_zero_pair
description: Calls a lower-level routine and makes one of two other lower-level calls, depending on whether its result is zero.

name: decode_bit_flags_to_value
description: Reads a bit pattern from a lower-level routine and maps its low bits to a shared value of minus one or one. Bit four also triggers a further lower-level call.

name: combine_status_flag_bytes
description: Combines the low bits of several status bytes into the shared value, setting it to minus one, zero or one depending on which bytes are set and in what order.

name: test_flag_bit_four_set
description: Returns zero when the shared value's low bit is clear and a lower-level routine's result lacks bit four. Otherwise it returns one.

name: call_with_local_buffer
description: Allocates a sixty-four byte local buffer, passes it with five arguments to a lower-level routine, then calls a second routine on the buffer.

name: call_routine_pair_no_args
description: Calls two lower-level routines with no arguments in succession.

name: reset_custom_chip_registers
description: Waits until a busy bit in a hardware status register clears, then writes constants to the audio channel, blitter control, and interrupt and DMA registers. It returns a zero word.

name: initialise_cia_registers
description: Writes a sequence of constants to the CIA chip registers, covering timer and port registers on both CIA chips. It returns thirty-one.

name: set_dma_enable_bits
description: Writes a constant with its top bit and bit six set to the DMA control register, enabling the DMA channels those bits name.

name: blit_region_in_chunks
description: Sets up blitter registers and splits a size value into blocks of up to four thousand ninety-six, passing each block to a lower-level routine. The control value depends on a flag argument.

name: setup_blitter_modulo_and_loop
description: Configures blitter control and modulo registers, choosing one of two control values from its flag argument. It then loops over a size in chunks of up to four thousand ninety-six and passes each chunk to a lower-level routine.

name: program_blitter_for_region
description: Converts a region's position and size into sixteen-pixel word columns and rows. It programs the blitter address and modulo registers from those values.

name: program_blitter_region_variant
description: Performs the same region-to-blitter computation as its neighbour with differently ordered parameters. It programs blitter address, modulo and control registers from word columns and row counts.

name: return_third_word_argument
description: Returns its third argument unchanged. The other arguments are unused.

name: build_copper_pointer_list
description: Fills ten consecutive slots with addresses spaced one hundred thirty-one thousand seventy-two bytes apart, followed by a terminator. It stores the address of the first slot in the shared variable and touches the copper list pointer register.

name: write_copper_address_pairs
description: Splits an address argument into high and low words and writes them into consecutive copper list entries. It also writes two further addresses offset by sixteen thousand and twenty-four thousand bytes, then triggers the copper jump register.

name: fill_interrupt_vector_table
description: Fills low-memory vector slots up to two hundred fifty-six with the address of a default handler, leaving one slot unchanged. It then sets a further group of entries to the same handler.

name: report_unexpected_exception
description: Passes the shared global variable address to a lower-level routine and returns. The handler references the text unexpected exception.

name: report_premature_interrupt
description: Passes the shared global variable address to a lower-level routine and returns. The handler references the text premature interrupt.

name: report_unexpected_trap
description: Passes the shared global variable address to a lower-level routine and returns. The referenced text is the message unexpected trap.

name: report_bus_error
description: Passes the shared global variable address to a lower-level routine and returns. The referenced text is the message bus error.

name: report_address_error
description: Passes the shared global variable address to a lower-level routine and returns. The referenced text is the message address error.

name: report_illegal_instruction
description: Passes the shared global variable address to a lower-level routine and returns. The referenced text is the message illegal instruction.

name: report_zero_divide
description: Passes the shared global variable address to a lower-level routine and returns. The referenced text is the message zero divide.

name: report_chk_instruction_trap
description: Passes the shared global variable address to a lower-level routine and returns. The referenced text names the CHK instruction exception.

name: report_trapv_instruction_trap
description: Passes the shared global variable address to a lower-level routine and returns. The referenced text names the TRAPV instruction exception.

name: report_privilege_violation
description: Passes the shared global variable address to a lower-level routine and returns. The referenced text is the message privilege violation.

name: report_trace_exception
description: Passes the shared global variable address to a lower-level routine and returns. The referenced text is the message trace exception.

name: report_spurious_interrupt
description: Passes the shared global variable address to a lower-level routine and returns. The referenced text is the message spurious interrupt.

name: install_default_handlers_and_enable
description: Stores a default handler in seven vector slots and makes four lower-level calls. It then writes constants to the interrupt enable setup, touching the CIA interrupt control and interrupt enable registers, and makes one more call.

name: disable_all_interrupts
description: Writes a constant with its top bit clear to the interrupt enable and request registers, which disables those interrupts. It returns thirty-one.

name: report_level1_interrupt
description: Stores seven in the shared variable, passes its address to a lower-level routine and returns. The referenced text is the message unexpected LEVEL1 interrupt.

name: dispatch_level2_interrupt_sources
description: Dispatches a level-two interrupt by testing bits of the saved status byte and calling lower-level routines for each bit set. The referenced text is the message unexpected LEVEL2 interrupt.

name: dispatch_level3_interrupt_bits
description: Tests three bits of the saved status byte. It calls lower-level routines for two of them and clears a stored word for the third, and the referenced text is the message unexpected LEVEL3 interrupt.

name: call_handler_no_args
description: Calls a lower-level routine with no arguments and returns, forming a thin interrupt entry point.

name: report_level5_interrupt
description: Stores six thousand one hundred forty-four in the shared variable, passes its address to a lower-level routine and returns. The referenced text is the message unexpected LEVEL5 interrupt.

name: dispatch_level6_interrupt_bits
description: Stores eight thousand one hundred ninety-two in the shared variable, then tests bits of the saved status byte and calls lower-level routines for those set. The referenced text is the message unexpected LEVEL6 interrupt.

name: report_level7_interrupt
description: Passes the shared global variable address to a lower-level routine and returns. The referenced text is the message unexpected LEVEL7 interrupt.

name: restore_saved_global_then_clear
description: Copies a saved value into the shared variable and then sets the variable to zero.

name: decrement_counter_and_call
description: Decrements the shared counter. When the counter has run out it reloads it from a saved value and makes a lower-level call, then makes one more lower-level call.

name: return_zero_after_self_compare
description: Its opening test compares the shared variable with itself, so the decompile always returns zero before the rest of the body. The unreachable body would advance a ten-slot index with wraparound and map table bytes in the sixty range to values.

name: send_chunks_of_sixteen
description: Passes a count down to a lower-level routine in chunks of at most sixteen. It stops early when that routine returns nonzero and returns that status, or returns zero when the count is zero.

name: send_chunks_limited_by_register
description: Repeatedly passes the smaller of a remaining count and a limit to a lower-level routine. It returns early with a nonzero status from a check call, and stops when the count reaches zero.

name: send_chunks_then_check_status
description: Variant of its neighbours that passes a chunk first and makes a status check on each pass. It returns the nonzero status when one appears.

name: send_chunks_check_loop_variant
description: Variant of its neighbours that sends a chunk, then checks status and adjusts the chunk size for the next pass. It returns the status once it is nonzero.

name: wait_until_status_clear
description: Calls a lower-level routine repeatedly until it returns zero, then returns zero.

name: mark_nine_entries_flag_bit
description: Clears five shared variables and makes a lower-level call on a fixed table with a length of one hundred twenty-eight. It then sets the top bit in table entries addressed by nine consecutive shared bytes.

name: shift_bits_into_serial_table
description: Builds a bit pattern from the shared value, records it in a flag table and an output table, and advances a counter that wraps at ten. The hardware register list names the CIA-A serial data and control registers.

name: forward_argument_to_routine
description: Passes its argument to a lower-level routine and returns.

name: forward_argument_to_routine
description: Passes its argument to a lower-level routine and returns. The body is identical to its neighbouring routine.

name: repeat_mode_one_until_zero
description: Repeatedly calls a lower-level routine with mode one and its arguments until the result is zero.

name: repeat_modes_two_then_three
description: Calls a lower-level routine with mode two and returns if that succeeds. Otherwise it calls it with mode three, repeating until a call returns zero.

name: store_timer_setup_fields
description: Dispatches on a mode argument. Mode zero calls a lower-level routine, and modes zero and one store the parameters into shared fields when a flag is clear. It returns zero when the flag blocks the write.

name: start_cia_timer_if_idle
description: Stores timer parameters into shared fields when the shared variable is zero, and returns whether it was zero. The referenced text is the message bad timer in start_timer.

name: control_timer_state_by_mode
description: Dispatches on a mode from zero to two. Modes zero and two call lower-level routines and clear bit zero of a shared flag, while mode one makes a single lower-level call.

name: stop_cia_a_timer_b
description: Calls a lower-level routine, clears bit zero of the shared control value and zeroes it, then calls a stored callback. It touches the CIA-A control register B.

name: stop_cia_a_timer_b
description: Calls a lower-level routine, clears bit zero of the shared control value and zeroes it, then calls a stored callback. The body is identical to its neighbouring routine.

name: stop_cia_b_timer
description: Calls a lower-level routine, clears bit zero of the shared control value and zeroes it, then calls a stored callback. The referenced text is the message bad timer in stop_timer.

name: clear_four_shared_values
description: Sets four shared variables to zero and returns.

name: run_and_clear_callback
description: If the stored callback pointer is set, clears it and calls it with a zero argument. Otherwise it returns.

name: run_and_clear_callback
description: If the stored callback pointer is set, clears it and calls it with a zero argument. The body is identical to its neighbouring routine.

name: call_null_callback_if_unset
description: When the stored callback is zero, it calls through that zero pointer. The decompile shows a call to address zero, which would fault if reached, so this is likely a dead or bad-data path.

name: call_null_callback_if_unset
description: When the stored callback is zero, it calls through that zero pointer. The body is identical to its neighbouring routine, so the same fault path applies.

name: query_channel_state_flag
description: Returns a status flag for a sound channel index from zero to five. It tests a shared value for the first four channels, and uses a combined test for the later cases.

name: report_bad_sound_channel_test
description: Passes the shared variable address to a lower-level routine and returns. The referenced text is the message bad channel in test sound.

name: configure_sound_channel_state
description: Dispatches on a channel code. For channel zero it resets the shared variables to one and one hundred twenty-eight when they were nonzero, then stores the channel parameters and calls a lower-level routine.

name: start_audio_channel_zero
description: Copies the channel parameters into a channel record, including a sample address, length, period and volume. It then computes a value from them and makes lower-level calls, and the hardware list names the channel zero location, length, period and volume registers.

name: start_audio_channel_one
description: Copies the channel parameters into a channel record, including a sample address, length, period and volume. It then computes a value from them and makes lower-level calls, and the hardware list names the channel one location, length, period and volume registers.

name: start_audio_channel_two
description: Copies the channel parameters into a channel record, including a sample address, length, period and volume. It then computes a value from them and makes lower-level calls, and the hardware list names the channel two location, length, period and volume registers.

name: start_audio_channel_three
description: Copies the channel parameters into a channel record, including a sample address, length, period and volume. It then computes a value from them and makes lower-level calls. The referenced text reports a bad channel id.

name: play_sound_on_channels
description: Dispatches a sound request on a channel index. For the middle indices it sets per-channel state values in shared variables, then makes many lower-level calls. It touches the location, length and volume registers of all four audio channels.

name: return_third_argument_long
description: Returns its third argument. The other arguments are unused.

name: compute_peak_channel_volume
description: Calls a lower-level routine, sets shared values to fifteen and one thousand nine hundred twenty, then computes the largest of several shared values, using zero where a value is unset. It touches the audio volume and DMA control registers.

name: set_channel_state_by_index
description: Dispatches on an audio channel index from zero to three. Each branch makes a lower-level call and stores that channel's state constants, such as a one-hot bit value and a channel mask, into shared variables.

name: stop_audio_channel_zero
description: Calls a lower-level routine, sets the shared state to channel zero's constants, then calls a stored callback. It touches the channel zero volume and DMA control registers.

name: stop_audio_channel_one
description: Calls a lower-level routine, sets the shared state to channel one's constants, then calls a stored callback. It touches the channel one volume and DMA control registers.

name: stop_audio_channel_two
description: Calls a lower-level routine, sets the shared state to channel two's constants, then calls a stored callback. It touches the channel two volume and DMA control registers.

name: stop_audio_channel_three
description: Calls a lower-level routine, sets the shared state to channel three's constants, then calls a stored callback. It touches the channel three volume and DMA control registers.

name: stop_channels_zero_and_one
description: Calls a lower-level routine, sets the shared state to the combined constants for channels zero and one, then calls a stored callback. The referenced text is the message bad channel in stop sound, and it touches the channel zero and one volume registers.

name: set_channel_volume_by_index
description: Dispatches on an audio channel index. For each channel it calls a lower-level routine, then stores the volume argument in a shared variable when that variable is nonzero and the channel's bit is set.

name: apply_volume_to_channel_zero
description: Calls a stored routine, then stores the volume argument when the shared value is nonzero and bit zero is set, and calls a lower-level routine. It touches the channel zero volume register.

name: apply_volume_to_channel_one
description: Calls a stored routine, then stores the volume argument when the shared value is nonzero and bit one is set, and calls a lower-level routine. It touches the channel one volume register.

name: apply_volume_to_channel_two
description: Calls a stored routine, then stores the volume argument when the shared value is nonzero and bit two is set, and calls a lower-level routine. It touches the channel two volume register.

name: apply_volume_to_channel_three
description: Calls a stored routine, then stores the volume argument when the shared value is nonzero and bit three is set, and calls a lower-level routine. It touches the channel three volume register. The referenced text is the message bad channel in set volume.

name: enable_audio_channel_zero_dma
description: When the shared value is nonzero, writes the channel zero bit to the DMA control register and then writes an interrupt-enable pattern for the same channel.

name: enable_audio_channel_one_dma
description: When the shared value is nonzero, writes the channel one bit to the DMA control register and then writes an interrupt-enable pattern for the same channel.

name: enable_audio_channel_two_dma
description: When the shared value is nonzero, writes the channel two bit to the DMA control register and then writes an interrupt-enable pattern for the same channel.

name: enable_audio_channel_three_dma
description: When the shared value is nonzero, writes the channel three bit to the DMA control register and then writes an interrupt-enable pattern for the same channel.

name: enable_channels_zero_and_one
description: When two shared values are nonzero, writes the bits for channels zero and one to the DMA control register and then writes an interrupt-enable pattern for both channels.

name: write_channels_zero_one_dma
description: Writes the bits for channels zero and one to the DMA control register and then writes an interrupt-enable pattern for both channels. It has no guard, unlike its conditional neighbour.

name: enable_channels_two_and_three
description: When two shared values are nonzero, writes the bits for channels two and three to the DMA control register and then writes an interrupt-enable pattern for both channels.

name: write_channels_two_three_dma
description: Writes the bits for channels two and three to the DMA control register and then writes an interrupt-enable pattern for both channels. It has no guard, unlike its conditional neighbour.

name: clear_four_audio_state_values
description: Sets four shared variables to zero and returns.

name: update_audio_channel_states
description: Combines two shared values and, when a flag bit is set, steps a countdown and resets per-channel state. It writes location, length and volume registers for all four audio channels and returns a combined value.

name: read_audio_table_word
description: Returns the word at the given index of a shared per-channel table.

name: exchange_table_word
description: Stores a new word into a per-channel table and into a shared variable, and returns the word it replaced.

name: load_audio_table_from_source
description: When its first argument is nonzero, obtains a source pointer from a lower-level routine. It then loops over the flag bits of its third argument, copying either the argument or the source words into a per-channel table and shared variables.

name: load_audio_channel_fields
description: Loads per-channel fields from a source record, or uses its second argument when the first is zero. It splits each table word into four-bit fields and stores them into several shared tables.

name: advance_audio_envelope_float
description: Adds a parameter to a shared counter and, while the counter is below one hundred, loops over the per-channel table using floating-point constants. It calls lower-level routines to update the audio channels.
